cards.explanation: The answer is Levites. Ezra looks among the people and priests and says, "…I found no Levites there." (Ezra 8:15). Priests and regular folks are in the camp, but the Levites are missing. Ezra notices the empty spot, friends, and that's where the next part of the story starts.

The answer is True. Ezra sends his team to Iddo and his kinsmen with a message that they should bring ministers "…for the house of our God." (Ezra 8:17). Iddo is the leader at Casiphia. It's a short message with a clear request, friends, and I respect that.

The answer is God's gracious hand on them. Ezra says, "…since the gracious hand of our God was upon us, they brought us Sherebiah…" and the others (Ezra 8:18). He points straight to God. Ezra could have patted himself on the back for his good message, friends, and he didn't.

The answer is False. Sherebiah comes with "…his sons and brothers, 18 men…" (Ezra 8:18). Nobody has to hum a lonely tune on this trip, friends. And Hashabiah shows up next with 20 men of his own (Ezra 8:19).

The answer is temple. The text says Ezra's team brings "…220 of the temple servants, all designated by name." (Ezra 8:20). David and the officials had appointed them to assist the Levites. Every one of them is on the list by name, friends, and I'd call that a well-kept guest book.

The answer is a fast. Ezra says, "…there by the Ahava Canal I proclaimed a fast, so that we might humble ourselves before our God…" (Ezra 8:21). They ask Him for a safe journey for themselves and their children, with all their possessions. A fast means going without food to seek God, friends, and the text says they fasted and petitioned Him (Ezra 8:23).

The answer is that he had told the king his God is gracious to all who seek Him. Ezra was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers because they had told him, "The hand of our God is gracious to all who seek Him, but His great anger is against all who forsake Him." (Ezra 8:22). That's the reason the text gives, friends. I think I'd be blushing too.

The answer is True. Ezra says, "So we fasted and petitioned our God about this, and He granted our request." (Ezra 8:23). They asked for a safe journey, and God said yes. That's a short verse with a big answer, friends.

The answer is silver and gold and sacred articles. Ezra says he "…weighed out to them the contribution of silver and gold and the articles…" (Ezra 8:25). The king, his counselors, his leaders and the Israelites there had all offered it for the house of God. That's a lot of weight to hand over, friends, so I hope those hands were strong.

The answer is False. Ezra tells the priests and Levites, "The silver and gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers." (Ezra 8:28). It's given freely, not owed to anyone. That's a different thing from a tax bill, friends, and anybody who's opened a tax envelope knows the difference.

The answer is to guard the treasure carefully. Ezra tells them, "Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in the chambers of the house of the LORD in Jerusalem…" (Ezra 8:29). Their job is to protect it all the way there. That's a serious assignment, friends, and no snack breaks mentioned.

The answer is False. Ezra says, "…the hand of our God was upon us to protect us from the hands of the enemies and bandits along the way." (Ezra 8:31). Then it's all weighed out in Jerusalem and verified by number and weight (Ezra 8:33-34). No stolen silver in the story, friends.

The answer is in the house of God. The text says, "On the fourth day, in the house of our God, we weighed out the silver and gold and sacred articles…" (Ezra 8:33). That's the very place Ezra said it was headed (Ezra 8:29). The treasure ends up at the place it was given for, friends.

The answer is weight. The text says, "Everything was verified by number and weight, and the total weight was recorded at that time." (Ezra 8:34). Nothing is left to guess. Counted, weighed and written down, friends, and I wish my cookie inventory was that tidy.

The answer is 12. The text says, "12 bulls for all Israel…" (Ezra 8:35). The 12 goes with "all Israel," and the sin offering has 12 male goats too. Same number showing up twice, friends, and I'd say that's no accident of the text.

The answer is True. Ezra 8:35 says the offering included "…a sin offering of 12 male goats." It sits right alongside the 12 bulls, 96 rams and 77 lambs, friends. And the verse ends by saying all of it "…was a burnt offering to the LORD."

The answer is that they assist the people and the house of God. The text says the satraps and governors "…proceeded to assist the people and the house of God." (Ezra 8:36). The king's edicts get handed over, and help follows. That's a happy ending for the paperwork, friends.
